_comment: Single source of truth for the Qt sources that the published trees were built
from. The BOM.json inside each published tree is a COPY of this, written by
It lives in its own repository and not inside a consumer's tree because the
watcher needs to read it from a workflow, and GITHUB_TOKEN cannot reach
another repository. Making this the origin also removes the cross-repo token
problem and the two-file drift that would come with it.
Commits are PINNED, not the branch tip. That is what makes 'Windows and Linux
ship the same Qt' true by construction instead of true only on the day
someone compiled. These are the commits the Arch Linux package builds

qtbase.note: QMimeDatabase: handle buggy type definitions with circular inheritance

versionLabelHow: 5.15.19+kde+r96 is not invented here. It is the label the Arch Linux
package carries, and Arch computes it with:
that is 96, so the label is 5.15.19+kde+r96. Arch's PKGBUILD pins that same
commit, and its static pkgver line reads r96 too.
The recipe CANNOT derive this on its own: it fetches per-commit archives
instead of cloning, so there is no git history to run rev-list against.
That is why it lives here, next to the commits it describes.

why: The KDE branch commit is NEWER than the 5.15.19 release tag. It carries
upstream commits that landed after that cut as well as the distro
backports, so calling it '5.15.19 + KDE patches' is imprecise: the
version string stays 5.15.19 because Qt does not bump it on the branch.
It is measurably different, not a naming quibble: this tree ships SQLite
3.49.1 and libpng 1.6.47, the official 5.15.19 tarball carries SQLite
queNoEs: '5.15.19 a secas' no describe este arbol: ese es MODULE_VERSION, lo que
declara qtbase/.qmake.conf y por eso loseen los DLL. La etiqueta del paquete
es 5.15.19+kde+r96, que declara que hay 96 commits de la rama detras del

consuming: The published trees are plain Qt prefixes: drop one next to your project and
point your build at it (CMake: -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<tree> ; qmake: use its
bin/qmake.exe). Nothing in them depends on this repository.
Each tree carries a BOM.json recording exactly what went into it, including
the per-module commit and the SHA-256 of the archive that commit produces.
That BOM is the provenance record, and it is generated, not hand written.
